basis: Re-derived independently. 000001_initial_schema.up.sql:639-653 declares dh_card_cache with demand_json, velocity_json, trend_json, saturation_json, price_distribution_json; 000033 adds character_name and no later migration touches the five. I enumerated every reference to the table with `git grep -n 'dh_card_cache' 06d9f8ce -- internal web/src scripts docs ':(exclude)internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations'` and read all five statements in internal/adapters/storage/postgres/dh_demand_repository.go (UpsertCardCache :34, GetCardCache :71, CardDataQualityStats :95, ListCardsMissingCharacter :111, ListCardCharacterQuality :143). Every one enumerates its columns explicitly and none names any of the five. Trap 2 checked on my own route: the only non-migration hits for demand_json/velocity_json/saturation_json are the dh_character_cache INSERT/SELECT at dh_demand_repository.go:188/213/234 and log-message string literals in internal/domain/demand/service.go; trend_json and price_distribution_json have no hit at all. The dynamic-SQL escape hatch is closed: `git grep -nE 'Sprintf\(.*(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|FROM|WHERE)' 06d9f8ce -- internal/adapters/storage/postgres` returns empty output, and the only `SELECT *` occurrences are over UNNEST, not over a table. Five dead columns established statically without a database.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Not an error in the defect claim, but a material omission the ticket must carry. This is a known, deliberately deferred follow-up of the baseline commit itself (SLA-41 / 06d9f8ce), not a discovery: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-08-demand-repository-typed-seam.md:16 and :2041 and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-demand-repository-typed-seam-design.md:236,469 state the columns are intentionally left in place and require that a Linear ticket for the drop already exist. The acceptance criteria are correct but incomplete on release sequencing: the plan records that rolling back the app image does NOT run down migrations (docs/OPERATIONS.md:87) and that this repository auto-deploys on push to main, so the drop migration must not ship in the same release as SLA-41 and must wait until that release is confirmed live and no longer rollback-eligible. A developer following AC 1-4 alone would not learn that. Phase 4 should also dedupe against the existing follow-up ticket.

basis: Re-derived independently, with Trap 2 as the explicit target. 000001_initial_schema.up.sql:453-461 declares api_rate_limits(provider, calls_last_minute, calls_last_hour, calls_last_day, last_429_at, blocked_until, updated_at); `git grep -n 'api_rate_limits' 06d9f8ce -- internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations` shows no later ALTER — only 000003's RLS enable and 000028's REVOKE target list. `git grep -n 'api_rate_limits' 06d9f8ce -- internal web/src ':(exclude)...migrations'` yields exactly two statements, both in api_tracker.go: the upsert at :107 naming (provider, blocked_until, last_429_at, updated_at) and `SELECT blocked_until FROM api_rate_limits` at :134-136 (read at /tmp dump of the file, lines 104-140). Neither names a counter. I then chased every calls_last_* hit to its subject: api_tracker.go:52 sits in a SELECT list whose FROM clause is api_usage_summary, and I read that view's definition at 000003_supabase_security_and_perf_fixes.up.sql:64-76 — it computes calls_last_hour as COUNT(CASE ...) over api_calls, a different table. price_refresh.go:131 is an observability.Int log key, a Go string, not SQL. So both hits the map attributed to the column are same-name collisions, exactly as the trap predicts, and none is a reference to api_rate_limits.calls_last_hour. Dynamic-SQL escape hatch closed by the same empty Sprintf grep as DB-001. Three columns never written, never read; they sit at DEFAULT 0.

Re-derived. The db-map's view records list seven views; 000035_drop_ai_advisor_tables.up.sql (read in full) drops ai_usage_by_operation and ai_usage_summary, leaving five in the final state, of which only api_usage_summary carries a consumer (api_tracker.go:53, verified while working DB-002). `git grep -nE '\bactive_sessions\b|\bexpired_sessions\b|\bapi_daily_summary\b|\bapi_hourly_distribution\b' 06d9f8ce -- internal web/src ':(exclude)internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations'` produced empty output — that empty output, not a file:line citation, is the absence evidence. Widening the pathspec to the whole tree while excluding the migrations directory and docs/audit adds only docs/SCHEMA.md:1051-1060 and one line of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-08-remove-azure-ai.md, i.e. documentation, not consumers. The mechanism is real and fully settleable statically — no database needed for the defect claim, so this is not unresolvable. 000001_initial_schema.up.sql:245-247 creates idx_campaign_purchases_dh_push_status as a PARTIAL index (WHERE dh_push_status != ''). 000003_supabase_security_and_perf_fixes.up.sql:282-284 issues CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS under the same name with a non-partial definition. I additionally checked the ordering inside 000003, which the finding does not: its Fix 5 drop list (lines 244-272) does NOT include this index, so the name is still present when Fix 6 runs and the statement is genuinely a no-op — had Fix 5 dropped it first the finding would have collapsed. 000003's down file drops the index at line 11 under 'Undo Fix 6' and never recreates it (grep for dh_push_status in that file returns only line 11), so a rollback to 000002 destroys an index 000001 owned and a re-apply yields the other definition. Downgrading because the stated consequence does not follow. The performance harm is argued from purchase_dh_query_store.go:101 and :325, and neither supports it: campaign_purchases.dh_push_status is declared TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' (000001:205), so the `p.dh_push_status IS NULL` branch at :101 is unreachable by construction and the COALESCE at :325 is a redundant wrapper that renders the predicate non-sargable for a plain btree index in either definition. Line 101 also sits inside a CASE in an aggregate, not a WHERE clause. The only equality filters on the column are :21 and :126 ('pending'), which the partial index serves. CountUnsoldByDHPushStatus (:58-71) is a whole-table GROUP BY with no filter on the column, so its AC item cannot show what it promises. The real defect is migration hygiene — one index name with two definitions and a down-migration that drops what it did not create — not a missing index on a 27%-of-query-time path.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The impact argument. It claims 'live queries filter on exactly the rows the partial predicate excludes (NULL or empty dh_push_status)'. dh_push_status is NOT NULL DEFAULT '' (000001_initial_schema.up.sql:205), so no row is ever NULL and the IS NULL branch is dead; the only excluded rows are '' rows, and no query in the repository filters on them with a sargable predicate. The intended non-partial index would therefore have delivered no measurable benefit over the partial one for any query at this baseline, so the ~27%-of-query-time framing carried over from 000003's comment does not attach to the gap. Acceptance criterion 4 is also unprovable as written: CountUnsoldByDHPushStatus contains no dh_push_status filter for an index to serve.

basis: Not unresolvable: the defect claim is containment, which is decidable from the DDL alone, and only the cost of each duplicate needs the database — the finding says so in its own exclusions. I re-derived all three containments from 000001_initial_schema.up.sql. (1) :366 idx_access_log_card(card_name, set_name, card_number, accessed_at DESC) and :367 idx_access_log_covering(same three, accessed_at ASC): with the three leading columns equality-pinned, a backward scan of either index over the matching contiguous range yields the other's ordering of accessed_at, so one serves both and the second is write amplification. 'covering' is a name only — there is no INCLUDE clause. (2) :590 PRIMARY KEY (suggestion_date, type, category, rank) and :591 idx_dh_suggestions_date(suggestion_date): strict leading prefix of the PK's implicit unique index. (3) :234 idx_purchases_campaign(campaign_id) and :236 idx_purchases_campaign_date(campaign_id, purchase_date DESC): strict leading prefix; campaign_purchases' PK is a single TEXT id (:157) so the PK does not additionally cover it, as the finding says. Final-state survival is the map's replay, not my search: all three carry no 'NOT in the final schema' note, and so do their retained counterparts idx_access_log_card and idx_purchases_campaign_date, so the proposed drops do not leave a table uncovered. The lens brief's standing caveat — an index's zero direct references proves nothing — is respected: this finding rests on containment against a surviving index, never on a reference count.

The defect holds for one of the two tables and I could not refute that half. I read 000021_drop_market_movers.down.sql in full: it recreates mm_card_mappings and mm_sales_comps with structure and one index, and `git grep -c -iE 'ROW LEVEL SECURITY|CREATE POLICY|REVOKE' 06d9f8ce -- .../000021_drop_market_movers.down.sql` returns empty output — no RLS statement of any kind. mm_card_mappings genuinely had a policy in the state 000021 destroyed (000003_supabase_security_and_perf_fixes.up.sql:173), and nothing in 000021.down restores it, so a sequential rollback to 000020 brings that table back without the RLS state it had. That is a real reversibility gap. Two qualifications that bound it. First, the security consequence is thin: the state being lost is 000003's `USING (true)` policy with no TO clause, which admits anon and authenticated anyway (this is exactly what 000027-000029 were written to correct), so what is lost is regime consistency, not an access boundary — low is the right severity. Second, and materially, the finding's second table does not support it (see below).
what_the_finding_got_wrong: mm_sales_comps never had RLS, so recreating it without RLS is a faithful reversal, not a regression. `git grep -n 'mm_sales_comps' 06d9f8ce -- internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations` shows it created by 000005_add_comp_sources.up.sql:2 with no RLS statement, dropped by 000021.up:8, and absent from 000027_rls_remaining_tables — which ran after 000021, when the table no longer existed. At the 000020 state that 000021.down is supposed to restore, mm_sales_comps had no RLS at all. This makes acceptance criteria 1 and 2 wrong as written: AC 1 demands rowsecurity = true for both tables, and AC 2 demands that neither anon nor authenticated hold any privilege on either recreated table — a state stricter than 000003's TO PUBLIC policy that mm_card_mappings actually had at 000020. Both contradict the finding's own exclusion, which correctly defends 000028.down's `USING (true)` recreation on the grounds that a down-migration's job is to restore the exact prior state. A developer working from these criteria alone would write a down-migration that also fails to reverse 000021, in the opposite direction. Hence ticketable: false — the defect is real and worth filing, but the acceptance criteria must be rewritten to cover mm_card_mappings only and to target 000003's actual policy shape before this can be handed to anyone.
